title: Tests something is recorded about
description: The repo's tests that some step of the journey has recorded something about, one entry each, so later steps work from this list instead of searching or running again. Each skill owns its own key, under found_by and in each entry, and replaces only that; an entry goes when no skill has anything left to record about it. Totals stay in testing/assessment.yaml. Kept as testing/tests.yaml.

found_by.description: For each skill that has written here, keyed by its name: its version, the commit it ran at, and in a repo with more than one module the modules it has covered so far.

modules.description: Each module's folder from the repo root.

test.description: Who the test is: the fully qualified class and method (com.example.orders.OrderRepositoryIT.findsAnOrder), or for a Cucumber scenario <feature file path>: <scenario title>, with ' (row <line>)' for an examples row. As JUnit's and Surefire's reports name it. Where two test folders hold a class of the same name, the one whose folder comes later in byte order adds ' (<folder>)', so both have an entry.

at.description: Where it is now: path:line, the path from the repo root and the line with the test's name. Each step that touches the entry refreshes it.

external_systems.description: Owned by draft-the-external-systems-list: each system on the external systems list the test may reach, how that was found, and whether the test can reach it from its own settings. Measurement confirms or clears what it may reach.

found_by.description: code-path: under-test-external-calls found a chain of calls from the test to where the connection is opened; test-code: the test's own code names the host; test-settings: a file the test loads names it (properties, YAML, Spring XML, Spring Boot's settings); airgap-report: the airgap agent refused the test a call to it, on another machine.

grade.description: reaches: measurement leaves the test out, and repair pairs it; may-reach: its one run under the airgap agent confirms or clears it; cannot-reach: it runs, and a call out is a miss of discovery.

reason.description: Why the grade: the test's settings give a host, or the address is known only at run time; or the chain calls a mock first, the test starts an embedded server of that kind, its settings give no address, or the address stays on the machine; or the airgap agent saw the call.

through_set_up.description: For code-path: the chain starts in the test's set-up methods or fields, not its own body.

via.description: For code-path: the chain from the test to the reach point, as Class.method steps joined by ' > '.

where.description: For test-code and test-settings: path:line of the line naming the host; for airgap-report: the file and line of the caller the agent reported.

meaningless.description: Owned by find-meaningless-and-unreliable-tests: why the test passes whatever the code does: it never runs (disabled, never-runs), can't fail (no-real-assertion, swallows-failures), or checks only its mocks (mocks-everything); the other-... kinds are ones the skill finds by reading. Measurement's planted bugs confirm or clear it.

unreliable.description: Owned by find-meaningless-and-unreliable-tests: why the test may give a different answer on another run: it sleeps for a fixed time, or depends on the order tests run in. Measurement's repeats in varied orders confirm or clear it.

measurement.description: Owned by measure-a-repo: what the test did when measurement ran it.

outcome.description: left-out: not run, because it reaches an external system; failed-every-run: failed in its run and in every rerun alone; flaky: passed and failed with nothing changed; order-dependent: failed in some orders and passed in every rerun alone. never-run: the build's test runner never runs it (a class its includes or excludes leave out, or a method it doesn't pick up), so no run measured it.

runs.description: Each run in order: P passed, F failed, S skipped (disabled), - not run.

reruns.description: A failed test's reruns alone, in order.

left_out_because.description: For left-out: the external system and the grade that left it out.

called.description: Each target the airgap agent refused for this test, as its report names it, sorted: only report lines with outcome refused, which are all on another machine, since the agent allows the machine itself.

missed_by_discovery.description: It called something off the machine that none of its external_systems entries names: discovery's searches missed it.

repair.description: Owned by the repair skill: what repair did with this test (decisions 0086, 0095, 0096). A test that reaches an external system and has no repair field is still to pair; the testing plan keeps a piece of work for its system until each such test has one.

state.description: paired: the test is now a pair, one run injecting the stand-in and one tagged external; waiting: it can't be paired yet, for the reason in waits_for.

pair.description: For paired: the class that holds the test bodies (a test interface, or the parameterised class on JUnit 4); then the stand-in half's class and any stand-in classes written for it; then the external half's class, or 'external target' for a parameterised class. As "<bodies>; stand-in: <classes>; external: <class or external target>".

waits_for.description: For waiting: why; the testing plan turns it into work. test-fails-on-its-own: the stand-in works but the test body fails whatever the stand-in does, so it would fail against the real system too.

pull_request.description: The pull request that made the change, or that a person turned down.

note.description: What the testing plan must know about this test's repair: why it waits, in a sentence, or something repair found but may not change, such as a build that leaves the stand-in half out of its normal runs.
